### Postman Collection
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/postman-collection

> Download the public SDP API Postman collection generated from the OpenAPI contract.

The Postman collection is generated from the same public OpenAPI contract that
powers the [API reference](/docs/reference/api). It includes every
end-user-facing family published there.

Internal-only endpoint families such as `rpc`, `admin`, `onboarding`, `auth`, `organizations`, and `members` are intentionally excluded.

<a href="/docs/postman/collection.json" download>Download Postman collection</a>
  <a href="/docs/postman/collection.json">Open raw JSON</a>

When you import the collection into Postman, set:

- `baseUrl` to the SDP API environment you want to target
- `sdpApiKey` to your bearer API key

Requests to routes that require an `Idempotency-Key` send a saved per-operation key, the `idempotencyKey.<operationId>` collection variable. The collection mints it when unset and clears it only after a `2xx` that shows the payment final, a replayed refusal, or a `422` rejection other than `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`. While a response shows the payment `pending` or `processing`, the key is kept: poll it with `GET` instead of sending a new one, and clear the variable once it is final. Resending after a timeout, a `5xx`, a `409`, a `429`, a `400`, `401` or `403` refusal, or a `422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED` keeps the same key. See [Idempotency](/docs/developing-with-sdp/idempotency#the-dashboard-and-the-postman-collection).

---

## Conventions

### API conventions
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/conventions

> What every SDP API call has in common, from how it authenticates to how it fails.

Every route follows the same rules, so learn them once:

- [Authentication](/docs/developing-with-sdp/authentication): send an API key in the `Authorization` header. Its grants decide what it can do.
- [Environments](/docs/developing-with-sdp#environments): a project runs in sandbox (devnet) or production (mainnet-beta), and its keys work in that environment only.
- [Idempotency](/docs/developing-with-sdp/idempotency): send an `Idempotency-Key` to retry a mutation safely. Routes that move money require one.
- [Errors](/docs/reference/conventions/errors): one error envelope, with a code to branch on.
- [Pagination](/docs/reference/conventions/pagination): lists return one page at a time.
- [Rate limits](/docs/reference/conventions/rate-limits): each API key gets a set number of requests per minute.
- [Versioning](/docs/reference/conventions/versioning): the version is in the path, and a breaking change gets a new one.

A successful JSON response wraps its payload in `data`, with `meta.requestId` beside it; a `204` has no body, and the health checks answer with their own. Every response also carries the ID in `X-Request-ID`: quote it when you report a problem.

---

### Errors
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/conventions/errors

> A failed request returns an HTTP error status and one error envelope, with a code to branch on.

A failed request returns an error status and this body. The health checks are the exception: each answers with its own body, as its page shows.

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "FORBIDDEN",
    "message": "Access denied"
  },
  "meta": { "requestId": "req_..." }
}
```

- `code` is stable: branch on it, not on `message`, which is for people and can change.
- `details`, when present, says more, such as which field failed validation.
- `meta.requestId` identifies the request. Quote it when you report a problem.

## Statuses

| Status | Means | Common codes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `400` | The request is malformed or fails validation. | `BAD_REQUEST`, `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED` |
| `401` | The API key is missing, invalid, expired or revoked. | `UNAUTHORIZED`, `INVALID_API_KEY` |
| `403` | The key lacks the grant or wallet access the request needs, or the call comes from an IP address the key doesn't allow. | `FORBIDDEN`, `INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS` |
| `404` | Nothing with that ID exists in the project. | `NOT_FOUND` |
| `409` | The request conflicts with the resource's state, or a request with the same idempotency key is still running. | `CONFLICT`, `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` |
| `422` | The request is well formed but can't go ahead: its idempotency key was used for a different request, or the signing provider refused the transaction. | `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`, `SIGNING_REJECTED` |
| `429` | Too many requests. See [Rate limits](/docs/reference/conventions/rate-limits). | `RATE_LIMITED` |
| `500` | Something failed inside SDP. | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |
| `502` | Solana RPC answered, but with an error SDP could not use. | `SOLANA_RPC_ERROR` |
| `503` | SDP, or a provider it depends on, is unavailable for now. | `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`, `RPC_UNAVAILABLE` |

Each operation's page lists the statuses it can return, with an example body for each.

## Retrying

- `400`, `401`, `403`, `404` and `422`: fix the request before you send it again.
- `409 CONFLICT`: read the resource's current state, then decide.
- `409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` and `429`: wait for `Retry-After`, then retry with the same `Idempotency-Key`.
- `503 RPC_UNAVAILABLE`: `details.reason` says why Solana RPC was unavailable. `upstream_unavailable` is temporary: wait for `Retry-After`, then retry as the `5xx` rule below says. `not_configured` and `cluster_mismatch` are SDP configuration problems that a retry won't fix; quote `meta.requestId` when you report one.
- `5xx`: most routes store the error and return it again to a same-key retry. Read the resource with `GET` to see whether the request took effect, then retry with a new key. On the routes that move money, a same-key retry runs again and never acts twice.

[Idempotency](/docs/developing-with-sdp/idempotency) covers what each retry returns.

---

### Pagination
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/conventions/pagination

> Lists return one page at a time, by page number on most routes and by cursor on a few.

Each list operation's page says which of the two it uses, with its default and largest page size.

## Page numbers

Most lists take `page` (from 1) and `pageSize`. The page's items are in `data`, and `meta` says where you are:

| Field | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `total` | Items across every page |
| `page` | This page's number |
| `pageSize` | Items per page |
| `hasMore` | Whether a later page exists |

Ask for the next `page` while `hasMore` is `true`.

## Cursors

A few lists take a `limit` instead and return a `nextCursor` with each page. Send it back in the cursor parameter the operation names, `cursor` or `before`, to get the next page; it's `null` on the last one.

---

### Rate limits
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/conventions/rate-limits

> Each API key gets a set number of requests per minute, by its tier, and responses usually say how many are left.

Requests count against a limit per minute. Under `/v1`, a request with an API key counts against that key's tier (keys start on `standard`), and one without a key counts against its IP address. Outside `/v1`, every request counts against its IP address, even one that sends a key. The health checks and a few public reads aren't limited.

| Caller | Requests per minute |
| --- | --- |
| An API key on the `standard` tier | 100 |
| An API key on the `elevated` tier | 500 |
| An API key on the `unlimited` tier | 10,000 |
| No API key, per IP address | 20 |

These are the general limits. Some operations also have a tighter quota of their own, counted per key (or signed-in member) and per organization, so they can return `429` before the key reaches its tier's limit. While SDP's counter store is unavailable, those operations refuse with `503` rather than run uncounted.

Responses usually say where you stand. The headers are left off while SDP's shared counter store is unavailable, so don't depend on them:

| Header | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `X-RateLimit-Limit` | Requests allowed per window |
| `X-RateLimit-Remaining` | Requests left in this window |
| `X-RateLimit-Reset` | When this window ends, in Unix seconds |

Past the limit, a request gets `429` with the code `RATE_LIMITED` and a `Retry-After` header. Wait that many seconds before you send it again.

---

### Versioning
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/conventions/versioning

> The API version is in every product route's path. /v1 is current, and a breaking change ships under a new major version.

Every product route's path starts with its version: `/v1` is the current contract. A breaking change ships under a new major version, such as `/v2`, never inside `/v1`. The health checks, `/health` and `/health/ready`, have no version.

The OpenAPI document's `info.version` counts revisions of that document for the current path version. It is not the API's version.

| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/health` | [Health check](/docs/reference/api/health/health-check.md) |

---

### Health check
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/health/health-check

> Returns service health and build metadata.

`GET /health`

Public: this route takes no API key.

## Responses

- **`200`** Service is healthy

  - **`status`** · `string` · required · always `ok`

    Health status.

  - **`timestamp`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

    Health check timestamp.

  - **`version`** · `string` · required · example `0.1.0`

    Service version.

  - **`environment`** · `string` · required · example `production`

    Runtime environment.

  - **`releaseChannel`** · `string` · required · one of `experimental`, `beta`, `stable` · example `experimental`

    Release channel: which modules this deployment runs.

## Example request

```bash tab="cURL"
curl 'https://api.solana.com/health'
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const res = await fetch("https://api.solana.com/health", {
  method: "GET"
});
```

```python tab="Python"
import requests

r = requests.get("https://api.solana.com/health")
```

## Example responses

```json tab="200"
{
  "status": "ok",
  "timestamp": "2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "environment": "production",
  "releaseChannel": "experimental"
}
```

---

### Readiness check
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/health/health-readiness

> Performs readiness checks for downstream dependencies.

`GET /health/ready`

Public: this route takes no API key.

## Responses

- **`200`** Service is ready

  - **`status`** · `string` · required · one of `ready`, `not_ready` · example `ready`

    Readiness status.

  - **`timestamp`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

    Readiness check timestamp.

  - **`revision`** · `string` · required · example `sdp-prod-api-public-00042-abc`

    Cloud Run revision serving the request, or `local` outside Cloud Run.

  - **`commit`** · `string` · required · example `0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567`

    Git commit the serving image was built from, or `local` when the image carries none.

  - **`checks`** · `object` · required

    Dependency health checks.

    - **`database`** · `string` · required · one of `ok`, `error` · example `ok`

      Database connectivity status.

    - **`redis`** · `string` · required · one of `ok`, `error` · example `ok`

      Redis connectivity status.

    - **`egress`** · `string` · one of `pending`, `ok`, `unverified` · example `ok`

      Outbound internet connectivity of this instance. `pending` (not ready) while a fresh instance waits for working egress, `ok` once an outbound call succeeded, `unverified` when it stopped waiting and serves anyway. Absent where the deployment does not wait for egress.

- **`503`** Service is not ready

  Same fields as `200`.

## Example request

```bash tab="cURL"
curl 'https://api.solana.com/health/ready'
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const res = await fetch("https://api.solana.com/health/ready", {
  method: "GET"
});
```

```python tab="Python"
import requests
```

### Initialize wallet signing
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/wallets/initialize-wallet-signing

> Sets up Managed custody for the project's named provider by creating its active signing configuration and first wallet.

`POST /v1/wallets/initialize`

Production projects use BYOK only: there this returns 403 with details.reason custody_mode_not_allowed, and wallets are created in a Custody Connection with POST /v1/wallets and connectionId.

Requires an [API key](/docs/developing-with-sdp/authentication) with the `wallets.configure` action.

## Headers

- **`x-project-id`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `prj_example`

  Selects the active project for this request. Required for Clerk (dashboard) callers. Ignored when authenticating with an API key, whose scope is fixed to the key's project.

- **`Idempotency-Key`** · `string` · pattern `^[\x20-\x7e]{1,255}$` · example `idempotency_example_12345`

  Optional, and honored when sent. 1-255 printable ASCII characters; send a UUID per logical operation and reuse it on every retry. Within 24 hours, a retry with the same key and the same request returns the stored status and body with the response header `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Keys are scoped to the credential: within 24 hours, the same key with a different request, or from a different credential, returns 422 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`; after that, the same key from a different credential runs as a new request. A rotated API key is a new credential, so after any rotation read the resource with GET to see whether the original request ran, and never resend a money request under the new credential without checking first. A key whose original request is still running returns 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` with `Retry-After`. A 400, 401, 403, 409 or 429 refusal is not stored, so the same key runs again once the cause is fixed. Access is checked before the key on every request, so a refused request never claims the key, and a credential that has since lost access to the named resource gets 403 instead of the stored response. A replay is a snapshot of the original response: read the current state with GET instead of sending the request again. If the original request never recorded its outcome (it crashed), a same-key retry gets 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` until 15 minutes plus the route's lease have passed since the original was sent (about 16 minutes, or about 20 for transfer batches), then 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` with no `Retry-After`, as does every later retry with that key: read the resource with GET to see whether it ran, then send again with a new key. A 5xx is stored and replayed like any other answer; retry it with a new key.

## Request body

`application/json` · required

Initialize wallet signing provider for the project resolved from the request context.

One of:

- **provider: "local"**

  - **`provider`** · `string` · required · always `local`

  - **`walletLabel`** · `string` · max length 100

- **provider: "fireblocks"**

  - **`provider`** · `string` · required · always `fireblocks`

  - **`walletLabel`** · `string` · max length 100

- **provider: "privy"**

  - **`provider`** · `string` · required · always `privy`

  - **`requestDelayMs`** · `integer` · min 0 · max 3000

  - **`walletLabel`** · `string` · max length 100

- **provider: "coinbase_cdp"**

  - **`provider`** · `string` · required · always `coinbase_cdp`

  - **`network`** · `string` · one of `solana`, `solana-devnet`

  - **`accountPolicy`** · `string` · pattern `^[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{12}$`

  - **`walletLabel`** · `string` · max length 100

- **provider: "para"**

  - **`provider`** · `string` · required · always `para`

  - **`requestDelayMs`** · `integer` · min 0 · max 3000

  - **`walletLabel`** · `string` · max length 100

- **provider: "turnkey"**

  - **`provider`** · `string` · required · always `turnkey`

  - **`requestDelayMs`** · `integer` · min 0 · max 3000

  - **`walletLabel`** · `string` · max length 100

- **provider: "dfns"**

  - **`provider`** · `string` · required · always `dfns`

  - **`network`** · `string` · one of `Solana`, `SolanaDevnet`

  - **`walletLabel`** · `string` · max length 100

- **provider: "ibm_haven"**

  - **`provider`** · `string` · required · always `ibm_haven`

  - **`network`** · `string` · one of `Solana`, `SolanaDevnet`

  - **`walletLabel`** · `string` · max length 100

- **provider: "anchorage"**

  - **`provider`** · `string` · required · always `anchorage`

  - **`walletLabel`** · `string` · max length 100

  - **`network`** · `string` · one of `solana`, `solana-devnet`

- **provider: "utila"**

  - **`provider`** · `string` · required · always `utila`

  - **`walletLabel`** · `string` · max length 100

## Responses

- **`201`** Wallet signing initialized

  - **`configId`** · `string` · required · example `cfg_example`

    Created wallet signing config ID.

  - **`publicKey`** · `string` · required · min length 32 · max length 44 · example `So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112`

    Public key of the provisioned root wallet.

  - **`walletId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `privy_wallet_123`

    Provider wallet ID of the provisioned root wallet.

- **`400`** Bad Request

  - **`error`** · `object` · required

    Standard error payload.

    - **`code`** · `string` · required

      Machine-readable error code.

    - **`message`** · `string` · required

      Human-readable error message.

    - **`details`** · `object`

      Optional error details for debugging.

      - **`*`** · `any`

  - **`meta`** · `object`

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

- **`401`** Unauthorized

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`403`** Forbidden. Requires the `wallets.configure` action: an API key must hold it (a module's `manage` or `execute` also covers its `read`), and a signed-in member's organization role must include it. Without it the error is INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS and `error.details.action` names the action. Any other 403 names its own reason. Forbidden: the caller lacks the route's action or the API key is wallet-scoped, or custody setup was refused. A refusal's details.reason names the failed check: custody_mode_not_allowed when a Production project names Managed custody (Production is BYOK only), custody_provider_not_in_release_channel, or provider_not_entitled.

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`404`** Not Found

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`409`** Conflict

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`422`** Unprocessable Entity

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`500`** Internal Server Error

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`503`** PROVIDER_NOT_CONFIGURED: the deployment holds no credentials for the provider in the project's environment (details.reason provider_not_configured).

  Same fields as `400`.

## Example request

```bash tab="cURL"
curl -X POST 'https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets/initialize' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SDP_API_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "provider": "local"
  }'
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const res = await fetch("https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets/initialize", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.SDP_API_KEY}`,
    "Idempotency-Key": crypto.randomUUID(),
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    "provider": "local"
  })
});
```

```python tab="Python"
import os, requests, uuid

r = requests.post("https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets/initialize",
  headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['SDP_API_KEY']}", "Idempotency-Key": str(uuid.uuid4())},
  json={
    "provider": "local"
  })
```

### Create wallet
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/wallets/create-wallet

> Provisions a new wallet under exactly one provider account: the project's Managed config for provider, or the Custody Connection named by connectionId.

`POST /v1/wallets`

A body naming both, or neither, is rejected with 400. With an Idempotency-Key, SDP never records a second wallet for one key: a retry returns the wallet an earlier attempt recorded, including after the 24-hour key window. Privy and Coinbase CDP also receive a request id derived from the key, so they dedupe at the provider. A provider failure is stored as a 503, and a new key is a new provider request. A 503 can mean the provider created the wallet before the error, and with a provider other than Privy or Coinbase CDP, a failure that left no SDP wallet row makes even the same key a new provider request after 24 hours: before any retry after an ambiguous failure, whatever the key, check GET /v1/wallets and, if the wallet is not there, the provider account. The provider request id and the recorded-wallet lookup both include the credential, so after an API key rotation, once the key's 24-hour record has expired, the same key under the new credential is a new provider request and can create a second wallet: after a rotation, list wallets with GET /v1/wallets and check the provider account before retrying a create.

Requires an [API key](/docs/developing-with-sdp/authentication) with the `wallets.manage` action.

## Headers

- **`x-project-id`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `prj_example`

  Selects the active project for this request. Required for Clerk (dashboard) callers. Ignored when authenticating with an API key, whose scope is fixed to the key's project.

- **`Idempotency-Key`** · `string` · pattern `^[\x20-\x7e]{1,255}$` · example `idempotency_example_12345`

  Optional, and honored when sent. 1-255 printable ASCII characters; send a UUID per logical operation and reuse it on every retry. Within 24 hours, a retry with the same key and the same request returns the stored status and body with the response header `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Keys are scoped to the credential: within 24 hours, the same key with a different request, or from a different credential, returns 422 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`; after that, the same key from a different credential runs as a new request. A rotated API key is a new credential, so after any rotation read the resource with GET to see whether the original request ran, and never resend a money request under the new credential without checking first. A key whose original request is still running returns 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` with `Retry-After`. A 400, 401, 403, 409 or 429 refusal is not stored, so the same key runs again once the cause is fixed. Access is checked before the key on every request, so a refused request never claims the key, and a credential that has since lost access to the named resource gets 403 instead of the stored response. A replay is a snapshot of the original response: read the current state with GET instead of sending the request again. If the original request never recorded its outcome (it crashed), a same-key retry gets 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` until 15 minutes plus the route's lease have passed since the original was sent (about 16 minutes, or about 20 for transfer batches), then takes over and is answered from the record it wrote. A 5xx is stored and replayed like any other answer; retry it with a new key.

## Request body

`application/json` · required

Create wallet request body. Names exactly one owner: provider (Managed config) or connectionId (Custody Connection); a body naming both, or neither, is rejected with 400.

Any of:

- **Create a wallet under the project's Managed config for provider.** · must not include `connectionId`

  - **`provider`** · `string` · required · one of `local`, `fireblocks`, `privy`, `coinbase_cdp`, `para`, `turnkey`, `dfns`, `ibm_haven`, `anchorage`, `utila` · example `privy`

    Provider whose Managed config owns the new wallet. A project holds one active config per provider.

  - **`label`** · `string` · max length 100 · example `Mint authority wallet`

    Optional label for the new wallet.

  - **`purpose`** · `string` · one of `transfer`, `mint_authority`, `freeze_authority`, `fee_payer` · default `transfer` · example `mint_authority`

    What the wallet is for. Defaults to `transfer`, the only purpose a payment, transfer batch or recurring payment can send from.

- **Create a wallet under a Custody Connection.** · must not include `provider`

  - **`connectionId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `cconn_123`

    Custody Connection (BYOK) that owns the new wallet.

  - **`label`** · `string` · max length 100 · example `Mint authority wallet`

    Optional label for the new wallet.

  - **`purpose`** · `string` · one of `transfer`, `mint_authority`, `freeze_authority`, `fee_payer` · default `transfer` · example `mint_authority`

    What the wallet is for. Defaults to `transfer`, the only purpose a payment, transfer batch or recurring payment can send from.

## Responses

- **`201`** Wallet created

  - **`data`** · `object` · required

    Created wallet response payload.

    - **`wallet`** · `object` · required

      Wallet details.

      - **`id`** · `string` · required · example `cw_example`

        Wallet record ID.

      - **`custodyConfigId`** · `string` · example `cfg_example`

        Owning custody configuration ID.

      - **`custodyConnectionId`** · `string` · example `cconn_example`

        Owning Custody Connection ID.

      - **`provider`** · `string` · one of `local`, `fireblocks`, `privy`, `coinbase_cdp`, `para`, `turnkey`, `dfns`, `ibm_haven`, `anchorage`, `utila` · example `privy`

        Wallet signing provider.

      - **`isRuntimeExecutionAllowed`** · `boolean` · required · example `true`

        Whether SDP currently permits attempting runtime execution through this wallet's owner. This is request-time admission, not Provider health or a success guarantee.

      - **`walletId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `privy_wallet_123`

        Provider wallet ID.

      - **`publicKey`** · `string` · required · min length 32 · max length 44 · example `So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112`

        Base58-encoded Solana address.

      - **`label`** · `string | null` · required · example `Root Signing Wallet`

        Optional wallet label.

      - **`purpose`** · `string | null` · required · one of `root`, `mint_authority`, `freeze_authority`, `fee_payer`, `transfer`, `dvp_settlement_authority` · example `root`

        Optional wallet purpose.

      - **`status`** · `string` · required · one of `active`, `inactive` · example `active`

        Wallet status.

      - **`createdAt`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

        ISO 8601 timestamp.

      - **`balances`** · `object[]`

        Tracked token balances when requested and successfully observed. Omitted when the balance lookup is unavailable; an empty array is a successful zero-token result.

        - **`token`** · `string` · required · example `USDC`

          Tracked token symbol.

        - **`mint`** · `string` · required · min length 32 · max length 44 · example `4zMMC9srt5Ri5X14GAgXhaHii3GnPAEERYPJgZJDncDU`

          Tracked token mint address.

        - **`amount`** · `string` · required · example `1250000`

          Raw token amount as a string.

        - **`uiAmount`** · `string` · required · example `1.25`

          Human-readable token balance.

        - **`decimals`** · `integer` · required · min 0 · example `6`

          Token decimals.

        - **`usdPrice`** · `number` · example `1`

          Resolved USD price per token when available.

        - **`usdValue`** · `number` · example `125.5`

          Resolved USD value of this balance when pricing is available.

      One of:

      - **Owned by a Managed config.** · must include `custodyConfigId` · must not include `custodyConnectionId`

      - **Owned by a Custody Connection.** · must include `custodyConnectionId` · must not include `custodyConfigId`

  - **`meta`** · `object` · required

    Response metadata.

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

    - **`timestamp`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

      ISO 8601 timestamp.

- **`400`** Bad Request

  - **`error`** · `object` · required

    Standard error payload.

    - **`code`** · `string` · required

      Machine-readable error code.

    - **`message`** · `string` · required

      Human-readable error message.

    - **`details`** · `object`

      Optional error details for debugging.

      - **`*`** · `any`

  - **`meta`** · `object`

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

- **`401`** Unauthorized

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`403`** Forbidden. Requires the `wallets.manage` action: an API key must hold it (a module's `manage` or `execute` also covers its `read`), and a signed-in member's organization role must include it. Without it the error is INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS and `error.details.action` names the action. Any other 403 names its own reason. Forbidden: the caller lacks the route's action or the API key is wallet-scoped, or the provider account was refused. A refusal's details.reason names the failed check: custody_mode_not_allowed when provider names a Managed config in a Production project (Production is BYOK only: create the wallet in a Custody Connection with connectionId), custody_provider_not_in_release_channel, or provider_not_entitled.

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`404`** Not Found

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`409`** Conflict

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`422`** Unprocessable Entity

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`500`** Internal Server Error

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`503`** Service Unavailable

  Same fields as `400`.

### Delete wallet
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/wallets/delete-wallet

> Deletes the wallet from its exact owning custody target when that Provider supports wallet deletion.

`DELETE /v1/wallets`

Provider, when supplied, is a consistency assertion.

Requires an [API key](/docs/developing-with-sdp/authentication) with the `wallets.execute` action.

## Headers

- **`x-project-id`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `prj_example`

  Selects the active project for this request. Required for Clerk (dashboard) callers. Ignored when authenticating with an API key, whose scope is fixed to the key's project.

- **`Idempotency-Key`** · `string` · pattern `^[\x20-\x7e]{1,255}$` · example `idempotency_example_12345`

  Optional, and honored when sent. 1-255 printable ASCII characters; send a UUID per logical operation and reuse it on every retry. Within 24 hours, a retry with the same key and the same request returns the stored status and body with the response header `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Keys are scoped to the credential: within 24 hours, the same key with a different request, or from a different credential, returns 422 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`; after that, the same key from a different credential runs as a new request. A rotated API key is a new credential, so after any rotation read the resource with GET to see whether the original request ran, and never resend a money request under the new credential without checking first. A key whose original request is still running returns 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` with `Retry-After`. A 400, 401, 403, 409 or 429 refusal is not stored, so the same key runs again once the cause is fixed. Access is checked before the key on every request, so a refused request never claims the key, and a credential that has since lost access to the named resource gets 403 instead of the stored response. A replay is a snapshot of the original response: read the current state with GET instead of sending the request again. If the original request never recorded its outcome (it crashed), a same-key retry gets 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` until 15 minutes plus the route's lease have passed since the original was sent (about 16 minutes, or about 20 for transfer batches), then 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` with no `Retry-After`, as does every later retry with that key: read the resource with GET to see whether it ran, then send again with a new key. A 5xx is stored and replayed like any other answer; retry it with a new key.

## Request body

`application/json` · required

Delete wallet request body.

- **`provider`** · `string` · one of `local`, `fireblocks`, `privy`, `coinbase_cdp`, `para`, `turnkey`, `dfns`, `ibm_haven`, `anchorage`, `utila` · example `anchorage`

  Optional consistency assertion for the Provider of the wallet being deleted.

- **`walletId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `anchorage_wallet_123`

  Provider wallet ID to delete from its exact owning target.

## Responses

- **`200`** Wallet deleted

  - **`data`** · `object` · required

    Delete wallet response payload.

    - **`walletId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `anchorage_wallet_123`

      Wallet ID that was deleted.

    - **`deleted`** · `boolean` · required · always `true` · example `true`

      Deletion confirmation flag.

  - **`meta`** · `object` · required

    Response metadata.

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

    - **`timestamp`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

      ISO 8601 timestamp.

- **`400`** Bad Request

  - **`error`** · `object` · required

    Standard error payload.

    - **`code`** · `string` · required

      Machine-readable error code.

    - **`message`** · `string` · required

      Human-readable error message.

    - **`details`** · `object`

      Optional error details for debugging.

      - **`*`** · `any`

  - **`meta`** · `object`

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

- **`401`** Unauthorized

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`403`** Forbidden. Requires the `wallets.execute` action: an API key must hold it (a module's `manage` or `execute` also covers its `read`), and a signed-in member's organization role must include it. Without it the error is INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS and `error.details.action` names the action. Any other 403 names its own reason.

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`404`** Not Found

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`409`** Conflict

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`422`** Unprocessable Entity

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`500`** Internal Server Error

  Same fields as `400`.

## Example request

```bash tab="cURL"
curl -X DELETE 'https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SDP_API_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "provider": "anchorage",
    "walletId": "anchorage_wallet_123"
  }'
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const res = await fetch("https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets", {
  method: "DELETE",
  headers: {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.SDP_API_KEY}`,
    "Idempotency-Key": crypto.randomUUID(),
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    "provider": "anchorage",
    "walletId": "anchorage_wallet_123"
  })
});
```

```python tab="Python"
import os, requests, uuid

r = requests.delete("https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets",
  headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['SDP_API_KEY']}", "Idempotency-Key": str(uuid.uuid4())},
  json={
    "provider": "anchorage",
    "walletId": "anchorage_wallet_123"
  })
```

### List wallets
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/wallets/list-wallets

> Lists active wallets under active Config and Connection owners, oldest first.

`GET /v1/wallets`

Provider narrows the list to one custody provider.

Requires an [API key](/docs/developing-with-sdp/authentication) with the `wallets.read` action.

## Query parameters

- **`provider`** · `string` · one of `local`, `fireblocks`, `privy`, `coinbase_cdp`, `para`, `turnkey`, `dfns`, `ibm_haven`, `anchorage`, `utila` · example `privy`

  Wallet signing provider.

- **`includeBalances`** · `boolean`

- **`view`** · `string` · always `summary`

## Headers

- **`x-project-id`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `prj_example`

  Selects the active project for this request. Required for Clerk (dashboard) callers. Ignored when authenticating with an API key, whose scope is fixed to the key's project.

## Responses

- **`200`** Wallets

  - **`data`** · `object` · required

    Wallets list response payload.

    - **`wallets`** · `object[]` · required

      Wallets.

      - **`id`** · `string` · required · example `cw_example`

        Wallet record ID.

      - **`custodyConfigId`** · `string` · example `cfg_example`

        Owning custody configuration ID.

      - **`custodyConnectionId`** · `string` · example `cconn_example`

        Owning Custody Connection ID.

      - **`provider`** · `string` · one of `local`, `fireblocks`, `privy`, `coinbase_cdp`, `para`, `turnkey`, `dfns`, `ibm_haven`, `anchorage`, `utila` · example `privy`

        Wallet signing provider.

      - **`isRuntimeExecutionAllowed`** · `boolean` · required · example `true`

        Whether SDP currently permits attempting runtime execution through this wallet's owner. This is request-time admission, not Provider health or a success guarantee.

      - **`walletId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `privy_wallet_123`

        Provider wallet ID.

      - **`publicKey`** · `string` · required · min length 32 · max length 44 · example `So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112`

        Base58-encoded Solana address.

      - **`label`** · `string | null` · required · example `Root Signing Wallet`

        Optional wallet label.

      - **`purpose`** · `string | null` · required · one of `root`, `mint_authority`, `freeze_authority`, `fee_payer`, `transfer`, `dvp_settlement_authority` · example `root`

        Optional wallet purpose.

      - **`status`** · `string` · required · one of `active`, `inactive` · example `active`

        Wallet status.

      - **`createdAt`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

        ISO 8601 timestamp.

      - **`balances`** · `object[]`

        Tracked token balances when requested and successfully observed. Omitted when the balance lookup is unavailable; an empty array is a successful zero-token result.

        - **`token`** · `string` · required · example `USDC`

          Tracked token symbol.

        - **`mint`** · `string` · required · min length 32 · max length 44 · example `4zMMC9srt5Ri5X14GAgXhaHii3GnPAEERYPJgZJDncDU`

          Tracked token mint address.

        - **`amount`** · `string` · required · example `1250000`

          Raw token amount as a string.

        - **`uiAmount`** · `string` · required · example `1.25`

          Human-readable token balance.

        - **`decimals`** · `integer` · required · min 0 · example `6`

          Token decimals.

        - **`usdPrice`** · `number` · example `1`

          Resolved USD price per token when available.

        - **`usdValue`** · `number` · example `125.5`

          Resolved USD value of this balance when pricing is available.

      One of:

      - **Owned by a Managed config.** · must include `custodyConfigId` · must not include `custodyConnectionId`

      - **Owned by a Custody Connection.** · must include `custodyConnectionId` · must not include `custodyConfigId`

  - **`meta`** · `object` · required

    Response metadata.

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

    - **`timestamp`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

      ISO 8601 timestamp.

- **`400`** Bad Request

  - **`error`** · `object` · required

    Standard error payload.

    - **`code`** · `string` · required

      Machine-readable error code.

    - **`message`** · `string` · required

      Human-readable error message.

    - **`details`** · `object`

      Optional error details for debugging.

      - **`*`** · `any`

  - **`meta`** · `object`

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

- **`401`** Unauthorized

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`403`** Forbidden. Requires the `wallets.read` action: an API key must hold it (a module's `manage` or `execute` also covers its `read`), and a signed-in member's organization role must include it. Without it the error is INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS and `error.details.action` names the action. Any other 403 names its own reason.

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`409`** Conflict

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`500`** Internal Server Error

  Same fields as `400`.

## Example request


`GET /v1/wallets/aggregate`

### Get wallet public key
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/wallets/get-wallet-public-key

> Returns the persisted public key for an exact active walletId. walletId is required (400 without it); an API key with selected wallets gets 404 for a wallet it does not list.

`GET /v1/wallets/public-key`

Resolution is DB-backed only.

Requires an [API key](/docs/developing-with-sdp/authentication) with the `wallets.read` action.

## Query parameters

- **`walletId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `privy_wallet_123`

## Headers

### Check signer via simulated memo transaction
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/wallets/check-wallet-signer

> Signs a server-authored memo message with the named wallet, verifies the signature, and simulates the transaction.

`POST /v1/wallets/signer-check`

Nothing is broadcast and no sponsorship is spent. The wallet is the only readonly signer and the request cannot supply memo text.

Requires an [API key](/docs/developing-with-sdp/authentication) with the `wallets.execute` action.

## Headers

- **`x-project-id`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `prj_example`

  Selects the active project for this request. Required for Clerk (dashboard) callers. Ignored when authenticating with an API key, whose scope is fixed to the key's project.

- **`Idempotency-Key`** · `string` · pattern `^[\x20-\x7e]{1,255}$` · example `idempotency_example_12345`

  Optional, and honored when sent. 1-255 printable ASCII characters; send a UUID per logical operation and reuse it on every retry. Within 24 hours, a retry with the same key and the same request returns the stored status and body with the response header `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Keys are scoped to the credential: within 24 hours, the same key with a different request, or from a different credential, returns 422 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`; after that, the same key from a different credential runs as a new request. A rotated API key is a new credential, so after any rotation read the resource with GET to see whether the original request ran, and never resend a money request under the new credential without checking first. A key whose original request is still running returns 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` with `Retry-After`. A 400, 401, 403, 409 or 429 refusal is not stored, so the same key runs again once the cause is fixed. Access is checked before the key on every request, so a refused request never claims the key, and a credential that has since lost access to the named resource gets 403 instead of the stored response. A replay is a snapshot of the original response: read the current state with GET instead of sending the request again. If the original request never recorded its outcome (it crashed), a same-key retry gets 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` until 15 minutes plus the route's lease have passed since the original was sent (about 16 minutes, or about 20 for transfer batches), then 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` with no `Retry-After`, as does every later retry with that key: read the resource with GET to see whether it ran, then send again with a new key. A 5xx is stored and replayed like any other answer; retry it with a new key.

## Request body

`application/json` · required

walletId is the Provider wallet ID to check, required. Ambiguous Provider IDs are rejected; the check uses the resolved exact custody wallet record, and an API key may check only a wallet within its wallet scope.

- **`walletId`** · `string` · required · min length 1

## Responses

- **`200`** Signer check verified in simulation

  - **`data`** · `object` · required

    Signer check response payload.

    - **`walletId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `privy_wallet_123`

      Resolved signing wallet ID.

    - **`walletAddress`** · `string` · required · min length 32 · max length 44 · example `So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112`

      Resolved signer address used for the check message.

    - **`feePayer`** · `string` · required · min length 32 · max length 44 · example `So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112`

      Funded fee payer address used in the simulated message; nothing is spent from it.

    - **`memo`** · `string` · required · example `SDP signer check 123e4567-e89b-42d3-a456-426614174000`

      Server-generated memo text in the simulated check message.

    - **`signature`** · `string` · required · example `sig_example`

      The custody wallet's Ed25519 signature over the check message, base58. Verified server-side and exercised in RPC simulation only — the check never broadcasts, so this signature does not exist on chain.

    - **`simulated`** · `boolean` · required · always `true`

      Always true: signer checks run in simulation and cannot spend sponsorship.

    - **`checkedAt`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2026-02-20T00:00:00.000Z`

      Timestamp recorded after the simulation succeeded.

  - **`meta`** · `object` · required

    Response metadata.

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

    - **`timestamp`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

      ISO 8601 timestamp.

- **`400`** Bad Request

  - **`error`** · `object` · required

    Standard error payload.

    - **`code`** · `string` · required

      Machine-readable error code.

    - **`message`** · `string` · required

      Human-readable error message.

    - **`details`** · `object`

      Optional error details for debugging.

      - **`*`** · `any`

  - **`meta`** · `object`

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

- **`401`** Unauthorized

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`403`** Forbidden. Requires the `wallets.execute` action: an API key must hold it (a module's `manage` or `execute` also covers its `read`), and a signed-in member's organization role must include it. Without it the error is INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS and `error.details.action` names the action. Any other 403 names its own reason.

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`404`** Not Found

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`409`** Conflict

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`422`** Unprocessable Entity

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`429`** Too Many Requests

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`500`** Internal Server Error

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`502`** Bad Gateway

  Same fields as `400`.

## Example request

```bash tab="cURL"
curl -X POST 'https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets/signer-check' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SDP_API_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "walletId": "privy_wallet_123"
  }'
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"

  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.SDP_API_KEY}`,
    "Idempotency-Key": crypto.randomUUID(),
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    "walletId": "privy_wallet_123"
  })
});
```

```python tab="Python"

  headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['SDP_API_KEY']}", "Idempotency-Key": str(uuid.uuid4())},
  json={
    "walletId": "privy_wallet_123"
  })
```

### Get wallet by ID
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/wallets/get-wallet-by-id

> Returns active wallet metadata, exact Config or Connection ownership, runtime execution admission, Provider, public key, and by default the current SOL balance.

`GET /v1/wallets/{walletId}`

If the balance read fails, returns 503 instead of a zero balance. Set includeBalance=false for a metadata-only read.

Requires an [API key](/docs/developing-with-sdp/authentication) with the `wallets.read` action.

## Path parameters

- **`walletId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `privy_wallet_123`

  Provider wallet ID — the `walletId` field returned by GET /v1/wallets.

## Query parameters

- **`includeBalance`** · `string` · one of `true`, `false` · example `false`

  Whether to resolve the current SOL balance. Defaults to true; false returns metadata without balance RPC or pricing calls.

## Headers

- **`x-project-id`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `prj_example`

  Selects the active project for this request. Required for Clerk (dashboard) callers. Ignored when authenticating with an API key, whose scope is fixed to the key's project.

## Responses

- **`200`** Wallet details

  - **`data`** · `object` · required

    Wallet details by ID response payload.

    - **`wallet`** · `object` · required

      Wallet details with provider and optional SOL balance.

      - **`id`** · `string` · required · example `cw_example`

        Wallet record ID.

      - **`custodyConfigId`** · `string` · example `cfg_example`

        Owning custody configuration ID.

      - **`custodyConnectionId`** · `string` · example `cconn_example`

        Owning Custody Connection ID.

      - **`provider`** · `string` · required · one of `local`, `fireblocks`, `privy`, `coinbase_cdp`, `para`, `turnkey`, `dfns`, `ibm_haven`, `anchorage`, `utila` · example `privy`

        Wallet custody provider.

      - **`isRuntimeExecutionAllowed`** · `boolean` · required · example `true`

        Whether SDP currently permits attempting runtime execution through this wallet's owner. This is request-time admission, not Provider health or a success guarantee.

      - **`walletId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `privy_wallet_123`

        Provider wallet ID.

      - **`publicKey`** · `string` · required · min length 32 · max length 44 · example `So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112`

        Base58-encoded Solana address.

      - **`label`** · `string | null` · required · example `Root Signing Wallet`

        Optional wallet label.

      - **`purpose`** · `string | null` · required · one of `root`, `mint_authority`, `freeze_authority`, `fee_payer`, `transfer`, `dvp_settlement_authority` · example `root`

        Optional wallet purpose.

      - **`status`** · `string` · required · one of `active`, `inactive` · example `active`

        Wallet status.

      - **`createdAt`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

        ISO 8601 timestamp.

      - **`balance`** · `object`

        Current SOL balance for the wallet public key. Omitted when includeBalance=false.

        - **`token`** · `string` · required · always `SOL` · example `SOL`

          Balance token symbol.

        - **`mint`** · `string` · required · example `So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112`

          Native SOL mint address.

        - **`amount`** · `string` · required · example `123456789`

          Raw lamports balance as a string.

        - **`uiAmount`** · `string` · required · example `0.123456789`

          Human-readable SOL balance.

        - **`decimals`** · `number` · required · always `9` · example `9`

          Token decimals for SOL.

      One of:

      - **Owned by a Managed config.** · must include `custodyConfigId` · must not include `custodyConnectionId`

      - **Owned by a Custody Connection.** · must include `custodyConnectionId` · must not include `custodyConfigId`

  - **`meta`** · `object` · required

    Response metadata.

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

    - **`timestamp`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

      ISO 8601 timestamp.

- **`401`** Unauthorized

  - **`error`** · `object` · required

    Standard error payload.

    - **`code`** · `string` · required

      Machine-readable error code.

    - **`message`** · `string` · required

      Human-readable error message.

    - **`details`** · `object`

      Optional error details for debugging.

      - **`*`** · `any`

  - **`meta`** · `object`

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

- **`403`** Forbidden. Requires the `wallets.read` action: an API key must hold it (a module's `manage` or `execute` also covers its `read`), and a signed-in member's organization role must include it. Without it the error is INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS and `error.details.action` names the action. Any other 403 names its own reason.

  Same fields as `401`.

- **`404`** Not Found

  Same fields as `401`.

- **`409`** Conflict

  Same fields as `401`.

- **`500`** Internal Server Error

  Same fields as `401`.

- **`503`** Service Unavailable

### Update wallet
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/wallets/update-wallet

> Updates the display label of an active wallet under its exact Config or Connection owner.

Access is checked before the key on every request, so a refused request never claims the key, and a credential that has since lost access to the named resource gets 403 instead of the stored response. A replay is a snapshot of the original response: read the current state with GET instead of sending the request again. If the original request never recorded its outcome (it crashed), a same-key retry gets 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` until 15 minutes plus the route's lease have passed since the original was sent (about 16 minutes, or about 20 for transfer batches), then 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` with no `Retry-After`, as does every later retry with that key: read the resource with GET to see whether it ran, then send again with a new key. A 5xx is stored and replayed like any other answer; retry it with a new key.

## Request body

`application/json` · required

Update wallet request body.

- **`label`** · `string | null` · max length 100 · example `Treasury signer`

  Optional wallet label. Set to null to clear the label.

## Responses

- **`200`** Wallet updated

  - **`data`** · `object` · required

    Created wallet response payload.

    - **`wallet`** · `object` · required

      Wallet details.

      - **`id`** · `string` · required · example `cw_example`

        Wallet record ID.

      - **`custodyConfigId`** · `string` · example `cfg_example`

        Owning custody configuration ID.

      - **`custodyConnectionId`** · `string` · example `cconn_example`

        Owning Custody Connection ID.

      - **`provider`** · `string` · one of `local`, `fireblocks`, `privy`, `coinbase_cdp`, `para`, `turnkey`, `dfns`, `ibm_haven`, `anchorage`, `utila` · example `privy`

        Wallet signing provider.

      - **`isRuntimeExecutionAllowed`** · `boolean` · required · example `true`

        Whether SDP currently permits attempting runtime execution through this wallet's owner. This is request-time admission, not Provider health or a success guarantee.

      - **`walletId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `privy_wallet_123`

        Provider wallet ID.

      - **`publicKey`** · `string` · required · min length 32 · max length 44 · example `So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112`

        Base58-encoded Solana address.

      - **`label`** · `string | null` · required · example `Root Signing Wallet`

        Optional wallet label.

      - **`purpose`** · `string | null` · required · one of `root`, `mint_authority`, `freeze_authority`, `fee_payer`, `transfer`, `dvp_settlement_authority` · example `root`

        Optional wallet purpose.

      - **`status`** · `string` · required · one of `active`, `inactive` · example `active`

        Wallet status.

      - **`createdAt`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

        ISO 8601 timestamp.

      - **`balances`** · `object[]`

        Tracked token balances when requested and successfully observed. Omitted when the balance lookup is unavailable; an empty array is a successful zero-token result.

        - **`token`** · `string` · required · example `USDC`

          Tracked token symbol.

        - **`mint`** · `string` · required · min length 32 · max length 44 · example `4zMMC9srt5Ri5X14GAgXhaHii3GnPAEERYPJgZJDncDU`

          Tracked token mint address.

        - **`amount`** · `string` · required · example `1250000`

          Raw token amount as a string.

        - **`uiAmount`** · `string` · required · example `1.25`

          Human-readable token balance.

        - **`decimals`** · `integer` · required · min 0 · example `6`

          Token decimals.

        - **`usdPrice`** · `number` · example `1`

          Resolved USD price per token when available.

        - **`usdValue`** · `number` · example `125.5`

          Resolved USD value of this balance when pricing is available.

      One of:

      - **Owned by a Managed config.** · must include `custodyConfigId` · must not include `custodyConnectionId`

      - **Owned by a Custody Connection.** · must include `custodyConnectionId` · must not include `custodyConfigId`

  - **`meta`** · `object` · required

    Response metadata.

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

    - **`timestamp`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

      ISO 8601 timestamp.

- **`400`** Bad Request

  - **`error`** · `object` · required

    Standard error payload.

    - **`code`** · `string` · required

      Machine-readable error code.

    - **`message`** · `string` · required

      Human-readable error message.

    - **`details`** · `object`

      Optional error details for debugging.

      - **`*`** · `any`

  - **`meta`** · `object`

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

- **`401`** Unauthorized

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`403`** Forbidden. Requires the `wallets.manage` action: an API key must hold it (a module's `manage` or `execute` also covers its `read`), and a signed-in member's organization role must include it. Without it the error is INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS and `error.details.action` names the action. Any other 403 names its own reason.

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`404`** Not Found

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`409`** Conflict

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`422`** Unprocessable Entity

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`500`** Internal Server Error

  Same fields as `400`.

## Example request

```bash tab="cURL"
curl -X PATCH 'https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets/privy_wallet_123' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SDP_API_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "label": "Treasury signer"
  }'
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const res = await fetch("https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets/privy_wallet_123", {
  method: "PATCH",
  headers: {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.SDP_API_KEY}`,
    "Idempotency-Key": crypto.randomUUID(),
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    "label": "Treasury signer"
  })
});
```

```python tab="Python"
import os, requests, uuid

r = requests.patch("https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets/privy_wallet_123",
  headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['SDP_API_KEY']}", "Idempotency-Key": str(uuid.uuid4())},
  json={
    "label": "Treasury signer"
  })
```

### Get project provider availability
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/projects/get-project-provider-availability

> Lists every provider this deployment's release channel publishes, with whether this project can use it, counting the deployment's provider credentials for the project's environment.

`GET /v1/projects/{projectId}/provider-availability`

The same rule gates every provider entry point, so a provider reported unavailable is refused there with 403, or 503 when the deployment does not hold its credentials. A project outside the caller's organization, or another project for a project-bound API key, returns 404.

Requires an [API key](/docs/developing-with-sdp/authentication) with the `projects.read` action.

## Path parameters

- **`projectId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `prj_example`

  Project identifier.

## Responses

- **`200`** Project provider availability

  - **`data`** · `object` · required

    Every provider this deployment's release channel publishes, with whether this project can use it; a provider the channel leaves out is omitted, matching this document. Custody entries list the custody modes the project can set the provider up in (empty when none) in `modes`, and each refused mode with the first failed check in `unavailableModes`; every other entry carries `available`, plus `reason` naming the first failed check when unavailable. A provider is available only when the deployment's release channel includes it, SDP currently offers it, the organization is entitled to it, and the deployment holds its credentials for the project's environment; the release channel offers the same providers to Sandbox and Production projects. Custody `modes` include `managed` only in a Sandbox project whose deployment holds the provider's credentials; `byok` runs on the organization's own credentials and is the only mode a Production project can use.

    - **`projectId`** · `string` · required

    - **`environment`** · `string` · required · one of `sandbox`, `production`

    - **`providers`** · `object[]` · required

      One of:

      - **family: "custody"**

        - **`family`** · `string` · required · always `custody`

        - **`provider`** · `string` · required · one of `local`, `fireblocks`, `privy`, `coinbase_cdp`, `para`, `turnkey`, `dfns`, `ibm_haven`, `anchorage`, `utila`

        - **`modes`** · `string[]` · required · each one of `managed`, `byok`

        - **`unavailableModes`** · `object[]` · required

          - **`mode`** · `string` · required · one of `managed`, `byok`

          - **`reason`** · `string` · required · one of `custody_provider_not_in_release_channel`, `custody_mode_not_allowed`, `provider_not_entitled`, `provider_not_in_release_channel`, `provider_not_offered`, `provider_not_configured`

      - **family: "compliance"**

        One of:

        - **available: true**

          - **`family`** · `string` · required · always `compliance`

          - **`provider`** · `string` · required · one of `range`, `elliptic`, `trm`, `chainalysis`

          - **`available`** · `boolean` · required · always `true`

        - **available: false**

          - **`family`** · `string` · required · always `compliance`

          - **`provider`** · `string` · required · one of `range`, `elliptic`, `trm`, `chainalysis`

          - **`available`** · `boolean` · required · always `false`

          - **`reason`** · `string` · required · one of `custody_provider_not_in_release_channel`, `custody_mode_not_allowed`, `provider_not_entitled`, `provider_not_in_release_channel`, `provider_not_offered`, `provider_not_configured`

      - **family: "ramps"**

        One of:

        - **available: true**

          - **`family`** · `string` · required · always `ramps`

          - **`provider`** · `string` · required · one of `moonpay`, `stripe`

          - **`available`** · `boolean` · required · always `true`

        - **available: false**

          - **`family`** · `string` · required · always `ramps`

          - **`provider`** · `string` · required · one of `moonpay`, `stripe`

          - **`available`** · `boolean` · required · always `false`

          - **`reason`** · `string` · required · one of `custody_provider_not_in_release_channel`, `custody_mode_not_allowed`, `provider_not_entitled`, `provider_not_in_release_channel`, `provider_not_offered`, `provider_not_configured`

  - **`meta`** · `object` · required

    Response metadata.

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

    - **`timestamp`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

      ISO 8601 timestamp.

- **`401`** Unauthorized

  - **`error`** · `object` · required

    Standard error payload.

    - **`code`** · `string` · required

      Machine-readable error code.

    - **`message`** · `string` · required

      Human-readable error message.

    - **`details`** · `object`

      Optional error details for debugging.

      - **`*`** · `any`

  - **`meta`** · `object`

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

- **`403`** Forbidden. Requires the `projects.read` action: an API key must hold it (a module's `manage` or `execute` also covers its `read`), and a signed-in member's organization role must include it. Without it the error is INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS and `error.details.action` names the action. Any other 403 names its own reason.

  Same fields as `401`.

- **`404`** Not Found

  Same fields as `401`.

- **`500`** Internal Server Error

  Same fields as `401`.

## Issuance: Templates

### List token templates
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/issuance/list-token-templates

> Returns all available token templates with their default configuration and supported extensions.

`GET /v1/issuance/templates`

Requires an [API key](/docs/developing-with-sdp/authentication) with the `issuance.read` action.

## Headers

- **`x-project-id`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `prj_example`

  Selects the active project for this request. Required for Clerk (dashboard) callers. Ignored when authenticating with an API key, whose scope is fixed to the key's project.

## Responses

- **`200`** Template list

  - **`data`** · `object` · required

    List templates response payload.

    - **`templates`** · `object[]` · required

      List of available token templates.

      - **`id`** · `string` · required · one of `stablecoin`, `arcade`, `tokenized-security`, `custom`, `rwa` · example `stablecoin`

        Token template identifier.

      - **`name`** · `string` · required · example `Stablecoin`

        Human-readable template name.

      - **`description`** · `string` · example `USD-backed stablecoins with compliance controls and privacy features`

        Template description and use case.

      - **`decimals`** · `integer` · required · example `6`

        Default decimals for the template.

      - **`maxDecimals`** · `integer` · required · example `18`

        Maximum allowed decimals for this template.

      - **`requiresAllowlist`** · `boolean` · required · example `true`

        Whether allowlists are required for this template by default.

      - **`allowlistOverridable`** · `boolean` · required · example `true`

        Whether allowlist enforcement can be disabled by request.

      - **`requiredExtensions`** · `string[]` · required · each one of `transferFee`, `interestBearing`, `permanentDelegate`, `pausable`, `nonTransferable`, `defaultAccountState`, `scaledUiAmount`, `transferHook` · each example `transferFee`

        Required Token-2022 extensions for this template.

      - **`availableExtensions`** · `string[]` · required · each one of `transferFee`, `interestBearing`, `permanentDelegate`, `pausable`, `nonTransferable`, `defaultAccountState`, `scaledUiAmount`, `transferHook` · each example `transferFee`

        Extensions that can be configured for this template.

      - **`defaultExtensions`** · `object` · required

        Default extension values used by this template.

        - **`*`** · `any`

  - **`meta`** · `object` · required

    Response metadata.

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

    - **`timestamp`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

      ISO 8601 timestamp.

- **`401`** Unauthorized

  - **`error`** · `object` · required

    Standard error payload.

    - **`code`** · `string` · required

      Machine-readable error code.

    - **`message`** · `string` · required

      Human-readable error message.

    - **`details`** · `object`

      Optional error details for debugging.

      - **`*`** · `any`

  - **`meta`** · `object`

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

- **`403`** Forbidden. Requires the `issuance.read` action: an API key must hold it (a module's `manage` or `execute` also covers its `read`), and a signed-in member's organization role must include it. Without it the error is INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS and `error.details.action` names the action. Any other 403 names its own reason.

  Same fields as `401`.

- **`500`** Internal Server Error

  Same fields as `401`.

### Get token template
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/issuance/get-token-template

> Returns details for a specific token template including default decimals, required extensions, and available overrides.

`GET /v1/issuance/templates/{templateId}`

Requires an [API key](/docs/developing-with-sdp/authentication) with the `issuance.read` action.

## Path parameters

- **`templateId`** · `string` · required · example `stablecoin`

  Template identifier.

## Headers

- **`x-project-id`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `prj_example`

  Selects the active project for this request. Required for Clerk (dashboard) callers. Ignored when authenticating with an API key, whose scope is fixed to the key's project.

## Responses

- **`200`** Template details

  - **`data`** · `object` · required

    Token template response payload.

    - **`template`** · `object` · required

      Template details.

      - **`id`** · `string` · required · one of `stablecoin`, `arcade`, `tokenized-security`, `custom`, `rwa` · example `stablecoin`

        Token template identifier.

      - **`name`** · `string` · required · example `Stablecoin`

        Human-readable template name.

      - **`description`** · `string` · example `USD-backed stablecoins with compliance controls and privacy features`

        Template description and use case.

      - **`decimals`** · `integer` · required · example `6`

        Default decimals for the template.

      - **`maxDecimals`** · `integer` · required · example `18`

        Maximum allowed decimals for this template.

      - **`requiresAllowlist`** · `boolean` · required · example `true`

        Whether allowlists are required for this template by default.

      - **`allowlistOverridable`** · `boolean` · required · example `true`

        Whether allowlist enforcement can be disabled by request.

      - **`requiredExtensions`** · `string[]` · required · each one of `transferFee`, `interestBearing`, `permanentDelegate`, `pausable`, `nonTransferable`, `defaultAccountState`, `scaledUiAmount`, `transferHook` · each example `transferFee`

        Required Token-2022 extensions for this template.

      - **`availableExtensions`** · `string[]` · required · each one of `transferFee`, `interestBearing`, `permanentDelegate`, `pausable`, `nonTransferable`, `defaultAccountState`, `scaledUiAmount`, `transferHook` · each example `transferFee`

        Extensions that can be configured for this template.

      - **`defaultExtensions`** · `object` · required

        Default extension values used by this template.

        - **`*`** · `any`

  - **`meta`** · `object` · required

    Response metadata.

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

    - **`timestamp`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

      ISO 8601 timestamp.

- **`401`** Unauthorized

  - **`error`** · `object` · required

    Standard error payload.

    - **`code`** · `string` · required

      Machine-readable error code.

    - **`message`** · `string` · required

      Human-readable error message.

    - **`details`** · `object`

      Optional error details for debugging.

      - **`*`** · `any`

  - **`meta`** · `object`

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

- **`403`** Forbidden. Requires the `issuance.read` action: an API key must hold it (a module's `manage` or `execute` also covers its `read`), and a signed-in member's organization role must include it. Without it the error is INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS and `error.details.action` names the action. Any other 403 names its own reason.

  Same fields as `401`.

- **`404`** Not Found

  Same fields as `401`.

- **`500`** Internal Server Error

  Same fields as `401`.

## Example request

```bash tab="cURL"
curl 'https://api.solana.com/v1/issuance/templates/stablecoin' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SDP_API_KEY"
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const res = await fetch("https://api.solana.com/v1/issuance/templates/stablecoin", {
  method: "GET",
  headers: {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.SDP_API_KEY}`
  }
});
```

```python tab="Python"
import os, requests

r = requests.get("https://api.solana.com/v1/issuance/templates/stablecoin",
  headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['SDP_API_KEY']}"})
```
